title: Staff Embedded Systems Security Engineer at true
full_text: Space is a warfighting domain. True Anomaly seeks those with the talent and ambition to build the technology that secures it. OUR MISSION True Anomaly delivers decisive capabilities for space superiority. We build autonomous spacecraft, advanced payloads, mission software, and space-based interceptors — enabling the U.S. and its Allies to secure the space environment and counter threats from the ultimate high ground. OUR VALUES Be the offset. We create asymmetric advantages with creativity and ingenuity. What would it take? We challenge assumptions to deliver ambitious results. It’s the people. Our team is our competitive advantage and we are better together. YOUR MISSION Embedded systems security for space operations poses unique challenges: remote systems that must operate in adversarial RF environments, resource- constrained hardware, and trade-offs between security and performance in real-time systems. As our Principal Embedded Systems Security Engineer, you’ll own the security of our spacecraft, radio systems, and hardware platforms. You’ll build security platforms and foundational services that enable our hardware and software teams to develop secure embedded systems by default. This role demands deep security expertise and the rigor that comes from engineering systems that cannot fail. As part of the Platform Security team, you’ll work hands-on across C++ flight software, embedded C firmware within microcontrollers and radiation-hardened SoCs, FPGA designs, and real-time operating systems. Your work will impact the spacecraft’s critical subsystems, from flight computer through command and control, RF, and payload. If you’ve secured systems where failure means loss of life or national security impact, you’ll understand the constraints and rigor required here. This is a hands-on technical leadership role combining deep hardware security expertise with strong software engineering skills. You will write production code and build the tooling, test frameworks, and security validation platforms that harden our embedded systems at scale. You’ll tackle novel security challenges that don’t have an established playbook as we aim to set the standard for space-based security. In our AI-native environment, you’ll use AI to accelerate your work and help solve the hard problems of embedded systems security. This position requires the ability to obtain and maintain a security clearance. Responsibilities Own the security architecture, threat modeling, and defensive controls for our spacecraft platform. This spans the flight computer, subsystem firmware, FPGA gateware, cryptographic implementations, and secure boot. Architect and build the security platforms, tooling, and foundational services that make secure-by-default the standard across flight software, firmware, and hardware configuration. Design and implement PKI for resource-constrained spacecraft, covering device authentication, firmware signing and verification, secure boot, lifecycle management, and secure key storage. Architect cryptographic and security implementations to meet stringent government standards, including FIPS 140-3, CNSA 2.0, and CCSDS Space Data Link Security (SDLS), and drive the migration to post-quantum cryptography across the platform. Secure the flight software build and deployment pipeline by hardening the tooling itself and protecting the supply-chain integrity of build outputs, dependencies, and third-party components. Secure our test environments against supply-chain attacks while keeping them representative of the flight security posture, so we can exercise on the ground the controls used to protect the spacecraft in orbit. Lead security assessments and penetration testing against our spacecraft, RF systems, and test environments. Drive the adoption of secure design practices across the organization, partnering with flight software, hardware, and test engineering teams to embed security into the full development and validation lifecycle. Tackle novel security challenges in space-based systems where established solutions don’t exist, and stay ahead of emerging embedded and RF threats to proactively harden our systems. Use AI to move faster — accelerating development, analyzing security data, and closing technical knowledge gaps. Required Qualifications Active security clearance, or the ability to obtain and maintain one. Deep, hands-on expertise in embedded, hardware, and firmware security — including hardware attack surfaces, side-channel and fault-injection attacks, firmware security, secure boot, and hardware security modules (HSMs). Strong software development skills in C and C++, plus solid engineering fundamentals (data structures, algorithms, API design, and debugging production systems) and comfort working across multiple languages and at low levels (assembly, firmware). Proven track record of building production security platforms, tooling, and foundational services used by hardware and embedded engineering teams. Deep, expert-level PKI knowledge with hands-on experience designing and operating PKI for embedded and resource-constrained systems —certificate-based device authentication, firmware signing certificate chains, secure boot PKI hierarchies, certificate provisioning and rotation for constrained devices (where rotation isn’t trivial, e.g., spacecraft in orbit), secure key storage, and HSM integration. Expert-level applied cryptography: implementing and reasoning about cryptographic systems to stringent government standards (FIPS 140-3, and familiarity with CNSA 2.0 and CCSDS SDLS), and experience with the practical challenges of post-quantum cryptography migration. Strong familiarity with common NIST publications (e.g., the 800-series). Experience applying security testing methodologies for hardware and firmware, and building the tooling and frameworks to automate that testing at scale across engineering teams. Demonstrated principal-level impact: setting security strategy and technical direction across an organization, independently identifying and prioritizing the risks that matter most, driving hardening initiatives end to end, raising the security bar and mentoring other engineers, thriving on ambiguous and novel problems, and influencing and aligning teams without direct authority. Preferred Qualifications Hands-on experience taking cryptographic modules through formal FIPS validation (CMVP), beyond implementing to the standard. Experience with real-time or safety-critical embedded systems — timing constraints, deterministic execution, interrupt handling, and the security implications of hard real-time requirements. Background in a regulated or high-assurance domain: aerospace, defense, avionics, medical devices, or industrial control systems. Hardware reverse engineering, firmware analysis, and cryptographic implementation experience. FPGA/VHDL security and RF/radio security. HIL/SIL test infrastructure and embedded Linux environments. Supply-chain security experience and a track record of hardening build pipelines for embedded/firmware systems. Cross-domain thinking that connects hardware security requirements to cloud infrastructure, network security, and system architecture. Evidence of practical, hands-on impact — published CVEs, security research or publications, conference talks, open-source contributions, or relevant projects Base Salary: $200,000-$305,000 Equity + Benefits including Health, Dental, Vision, HRA/HSA options, PTO and paid holidays, 401K, Parental Leave Your actual level and base salary will be determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on the following considerations: job-related knowledge and skills, education, location, and experience. ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS Work Location —this role will be onsite at our Denver, CO or Long Beach, CA offices. The expectation is a minimum of 3 days per week in the office. Work environment —the work environment; temperature, noise level, inside or outside, or other factors that will affect the person’s working conditions while performing the job. Physical demands —the physical demands of the job, including bending, sitting, lifting and driving. This position will be open until it is successfully filled. To submit your application, please follow the directions below. #LI-Onsite To conform to U.S. Government space technology export regulations, including the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) you must be a U.S. citizen, lawful permanent resident of the U.S., protected individual as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3), or eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. True Anomaly is committed to equal employment opportunity on any basis protected by applicable state and federal laws. If you have a disability or additional need that requires accommodation, please do not hesitate to let us.

title: Content Writer (Remote, £31-33k) at Ellipsis®
full_text: Ellipsis is emerging as a market leader in “GEO” for B2B technology companies. This is a high-impact, varied role in a fast-moving and ambitious agency. The transition to AI search has put a lot of the SEO industry on the back foot. Ellipsis has always been consultative/strategic in our approach; we started building AI search products in 2021 on GPT-2, and thus this has been a time for us to thrive. Today, we think we have a better understanding of AI search than almost anyone else. We have both the tracking product (built in-house), the data (~25 million AI answers for analysis, with more tracked weekly), and the execution end-to-end from strategy, to writing, to in-house design, to optimization, and performance reporting. As the newest member of our in-house Writing team, you will craft outstanding content for our clients that uses – and feeds into – our latest AI search research. Content quality is extremely important to us! For the writer who can think strategically, learn quickly, and execute across a variety of subject matters (typically SaaS/tech), this is the dream role. What you’ll do The heart of this role is the content creation itself – taking a brief and working with a combination of your own skill and our cutting-edge AI tooling to turn it into a genuinely good piece of content. You’ll work on a varied mix of content for your assigned portfolio of clients, including (but not limited to) landing pages, informational content, comparison pieces, and listicles. Every article we produce needs to win the trust of readers, capture the voice of the brand, and be built to perform in both AI Search (GEO) and legacy search. You don’t need to be an expert in GEO from day one, but you’ll need a genuine interest in how it works and the ability to learn quickly, because it shapes how we build every content piece. Ellipsis uses AI in the writing process, and we produce a high volume of content. Ellipsis is also extremely anti-slop! Your job as a writer will be to use our custom AI tooling and craft high-quality and strategically impactful work that leverages Ellipsis’ very latest research on how AI search actually works. We are continually improving our processes and tooling, and you will be expected to feed back on what works (and what doesn’t) so we can get better faster. To succeed in this role, you need to be comfortable with leveraging AI for the parts of the writing process it’s great at, then build on top of this. AI handles the groundwork; your judgment and skill is what lifts the output above what any tool produces on its own. You’ll still have plenty of room for craft and creativity – deciding what’s actually good is the part we can’t automate. Communication, both with clients and the wider team, is also a core part of the role. You will be joining a small but growing team of four writers, and will work closely with our Content, Strategy, and Design teams. While you won’t own or manage client relationships directly, nor will you attend every check-in call, deeply understanding your clients’ products, audiences, and goals will be critical to creating effective content. You’ll need to be confident in gathering the information you need from clients and the internal team through onboarding calls, check-ins, and asynchronous communication. Our customers are predominantly B2B technology companies. We work with a lot of startups and scale-ups; B2B tech has been our bread-and-butter although we are also having success with B2C and have some very high profile clients in this area. The range of topics you’ll work on will be wide, and you’ll thus need to be confident with context switching and picking up varying styles and requirements across different clients quickly. As a 100% remote team, we carefully balance collaboration with an environment that enables everyone to do their best work. You’ll communicate with the team through Basecamp, our project management software, and Google Meet. The majority of the team is located in Europe, and you’ll be expected to regularly attend meetings between 10am–3pm GMT, with occasional calls outside these times. We’re looking for an experienced writer who can work well both independently and as part of a team. We’d expect at least 2-4 years of writing and editing experience. Excellent writing and grammar, and the discipline to fact-check every stat, price, and claim against primary sources are hard requirements. You’ll need to be confident in getting up to speed fast on unfamiliar B2B and SaaS topics and turn them into compelling, user-friendly content. A working understanding of GEO would be an advantage, but what we’re really looking for is somebody with an eagerness to learn and the ability to do so quickly. Strong critical thinking is a must-have at Ellipsis! You’ll need to be confident weighing sources, questioning a brief that doesn’t add up, and making sound editorial judgement calls without constant guidance. We are looking for writers who can spot gaps or friction within our current processes and systems, and help drive forward improvements. The ideal candidate will also be able to demonstrate the following soft skills: Proven organisational skills: You must be obsessive with deadlines, managing and updating tasks, and totally reliable. Fantastic communication skills: Remote work relies on mutual trust, so frequent and clear written communication is essential. Receptive to feedback with no ego and solutions-oriented: You can take an edit or a critique, act on it, and get better. At Ellipsis, continuous improvement is more important than being right. High level of self-awareness, a “people person”: You’ll be dealing with members of the team on a daily basis, so this is an integral part of the role. Self-driven work ethic: You need to be self-motivated, comfortable taking the initiative, and see projects through to completion. This is a full-time, 100% remote role. You’ll be a full team member, and involved in our team projects, work, and meetups. £31-33k/year salary, depending on experience, with pension benchmarked to UK rates. 28 days of paid holiday, with an additional 1 paid holiday day a year with each year of tenure, up to a maximum of 5 additional days. 4-day work week, once a month. Genuinely flexible working. Regular team retreats (~1 per year); last was Istanbul, previously in Edinburgh, Oxford, Madrid, and Budapest. Time and budget for learning and development. Enhanced maternity/paternity leave, and sick pay. Application process It’s important we find the best candidate for this position, and our selection process will reflect this. You’ll be required to attend at least three interviews (by video call) and carry out a (paid) freelance project with us before we make an employment offer. Much of our company Wiki is externally accessible, and you’re encouraged to read through this before applying. We have a very useful guide to our interview process available here. This tells you what we’re looking for and reading this will significantly increase your chance of success! Please apply through Workable: https://apply.workable.com/getellipsis. We will decide who progresses to the next stage based on the form you submit, your cover letter, and your CV. Please give us a good reason to select you! Taking the time to research the role, what we’re looking for, what we do, and what you can do for us will increase your chance of success. Your cover letter is where you have the space to do this. Whilst we love technology and sit at the leading edge of its adoption (we automate hundreds of thousands of actions a month internally), we want to hear from you rather than from ChatGPT. That might sound odd given how much AI is in the work itself – so to be clear: we use AI heavily day to day, but your application is where we want to see how you think, in your own words. The deadline for submission is the end of the day, on 30th September 2026. We’ll be in touch with all candidates following the close of applications. We do great work for clients and are building an ethical business that lets everyone do their best work. If you think you could be the next person to join our team, please apply!

title: NetSuite Systems Engineer at DoiT
full_text: Location As a Financial Systems Engineer, you will be part of Business Systems Engineering, a group of several teams that builds and runs the systems the company operates on. This role is based remotely in the United States (Eastern time zone), the UK, or Ireland. Who We Are DoiT is a global technology company that works with cloud-driven organizations to leverage the cloud to drive business growth and innovation. We combine data, technology, and human expertise to ensure our customers are operating in a well-architected and scalable state - from planning to production. Delivering DoiT Cloud Intelligence, the only solution that integrates advanced technology with human intelligence, we help our customers solve complex multi-cloud problems and drive efficiency. With decades of multicloud experience, we have specializations in Kubernetes, GenAI, CloudOps, and more. An award-winning strategic partner of AWS, Google Cloud, Microsoft Azure and Ingram Micro, we work alongside more than 4,000 customers worldwide. The Opportunity We are modernizing how we run our financial systems and bringing this work in-house, and we’re looking for a Financial Systems Engineer to own it. You will own our financial systems - NetSuite today, with FloQast and Ramp coming online - as an engineer, not just an administrator. What sets this role apart is mindset. You are the kind of person who is averse to doing the same manual task twice and instinctively looks for ways to automate it away. You will own the configuration and business logic of the financial systems, keeping each one doing what it does best, and partner with our internal engineering team on cross-system integration rather than wiring it together by hand. This is a high-ownership role serving Finance and Accounting directly. You will be their dedicated systems partner - someone who knows the platforms deeply, is invested in making them better, and treats reducing manual, error-prone work as the core of the job rather than something to do on the side. Reporting to the Manager of Enterprise Systems, you will have real room to shape how finance operations run as the company scales Responsibilities Own and administer our core financial systems - NetSuite today, with FloQast and Ramp coming online - including configuration, business logic, and day-to-day system health. Identify manual, recurring, or error-prone finance operations (month-end close, reconciliations, reporting, procure-to-pay) and reduce or remove them through automation, choosing the simplest effective approach and partnering with engineering for heavier builds. Serve as the business-logic and data expert for the finance domain, partnering with engineering to define and maintain the rules and canonical definitions the systems rely on. Build cross-system integrations on a central, version-controlled, observable integration platform in partnership with engineering, rather than as one-off scripts buried inside individual tools. Act as the dedicated systems partner to Finance and Accounting: translate their needs into system capability, own those working relationships, and serve as the technical owner for financial-vendor onboarding, configuration, and administration. Use modern AI tooling to draft automations and accelerate routine system work, amplifying your output rather than adding manual effort. Qualifications 3-6 years administering a financial or ERP system, with hands-on NetSuite administration required, including: configuration, customization, user access, roles, permissions, and workflows; core modules such as General Ledger, Advanced Revenue Management, Accounts, and subsidiary / multi-location structures; designing and implementing custom records, fields, and automations; building SuiteFlow automations in response to changing business needs; managing the NetSuite integration ecosystem. A working understanding of core finance and accounting processes: month-end close, reconciliation, accounts payable / procure-to-pay, and revenue. A strong drive to eliminate repetitive manual work, with a demonstrated track record of automating it (e.g. scripting, saved searches, workflow automation, or low-code/iPaaS tools). Sound judgment about where logic belongs - what should be system configuration, what should be a cross-system integration, and which system is the source of truth for a given piece of data. Comfort with at least one of SuiteScript, SQL, general scripting, or API-based automation, and the ability to read and reason about integrations even when engineering builds them. Strong collaboration and communication across both finance and engineering teams, with the ability to translate between them. Fluent English; knowledge of any other language is an advantage. Bonus Points: FloQast and/or Ramp administration experience. Experience working against a central integration platform or in an event-driven environment. Comfort using AI coding and automation tools in day-to-day work. Depth in SuiteScript (1.0 / 2.0), RESTlets, or NetSuite web services. Are you a Do’er? Be your truest self. Work on your terms. Make a difference. We are home to a global team of incredible talent who work remotely and have the flexibility to have a schedule that balances your work and home life. We embrace and support leveling up your skills professionally and personally. What does being a Do’er mean? We’re all about being entrepreneurial, pursuing knowledge, and having fun! Click here to learn more about our core values. Sounds too good to be true? Check out our Glassdoor Page. We thought so too, but we’re here and happy we hit that ‘apply’ button. Full-time employee benefits include: Unlimited Vacation Flexible Working Options Health Insurance Parental Leave Employee Stock Option Plan Home Office Allowance Professional Development Stipend Peer Recognition Program Many Do’ers, One Team DoiT unites as Many Do’ers, One Team , where diversity is more than a goal—it’s our strength. We actively cultivate an inclusive, equitable workplace, recognizing that each unique perspective enhances our innovation. By celebrating differences, we create an environment where every individual feels valued, contributing to our collective success. #LI-Remote

title: Senior Manager, Actuarial Strategic Operations at Clover Health
full_text: The Finance team at Clover Health is a group of strategic partners providing financial and operational insights that drive informed decision-making and efficient capital allocation. Guided by our core values of excellence, accountability, and collaboration, we provide actionable recommendations to improve health outcomes and reduce costs while ensuring financial integrity and innovation. The MA Plan Actuarial Strategic Operations team serves as the operational and financial nerve center for Clover’s Medicare Advantage business. Embedded within the Actuarial organization, the team combines deep business expertise with advanced analytics and AI to integrate financial, operational, and actuarial insights, monitor enterprise performance, evaluate strategic initiatives, and deliver timely recommendations that improve affordability, member outcomes, and financial performance. At Clover, AI is part of how we work. We expect leaders to thoughtfully incorporate tools such as Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, and emerging enterprise AI technologies into their daily workflows to improve analytical quality, accelerate execution, and enable better decisions. The Senior Manager, Actuarial Strategic Operations serves as the strategic and people leader of Clover’s MA Plan Command Center, leading a team of Actuarial and financial operations professionals responsible for governance, initiative portfolio management, financial integration, performance monitoring, and enterprise decision support across Medicare Advantage. This role partners across Finance, Actuarial, Clinical, Revenue, Pharmacy, and Operations to assess drivers of performance, align strategy, and ensure enterprise initiatives deliver expected outcomes. As a leader of the Command Center, you will champion automation and AI-enabled ways of working that enhance analytical workflows, reporting, and executive decision support. This role is accountable for the performance, development, and capacity of the Command Center team. The Senior Manager will translate enterprise priorities into clear team objectives, allocate resources across high-impact work, establish quality and execution standards, and develop the team’s financial, analytical, business partnership, and AI-enabled capabilities. As a Senior Manager, Actuarial Strategic Operations, you will: Lead the MA Plan Command Center Operating Model: Set the direction and operating standards for Actuarial Strategic Operations, including governance, initiative portfolio management, prioritization, valuation, execution tracking, executive reporting, and continuous improvement of analytical and AI-enabled workflows. Translate enterprise priorities into clear team goals, allocate resources based on business impact and capacity, and ensure the team delivers timely, high-quality decision support. Own Enterprise Performance Monitoring: Lead the team in developing and continuously evolving enterprise performance monitoring frameworks using leading and lagging indicators, dashboards, and KPIs. Establish analytical and quality standards, ensure consistent application across functional areas, and use performance trends to identify risks, prioritize team work, and guide leadership decisions. Lead Financial Integration, AI-Enabled Analysis, and Executive Decision Support: Set the standards for integrating operational, actuarial, and financial performance into clear recommendations for executive leadership. Lead the team in adopting responsible AI-enabled analytical methods that improve speed, rigor, scalability, and decision quality while maintaining appropriate governance, data integrity, and financial discipline. Ensure analyses challenge strategic assumptions, surface material risks and opportunities, and provide actionable options that support enterprise priorities and financial objectives. Drive Cross-Functional Alignment: Serve as the senior Command Center partner to leaders across Finance, Actuarial, Medical Economics, Clinical Operations, Revenue, Pharmacy, Product, and Analytics. Establish clear ownership, decision rights, and accountability across initiatives, resolve competing priorities, and ensure the team’s work is aligned with budgeting, forecasting, strategic planning, and enterprise performance objectives. Scale the Command Center Capability: Lead the team in expanding automation, standardizing processes, strengthening data quality, and implementing AI-enabled solutions that improve reporting, accelerate analysis, reduce manual effort, and scale the Command Center operating model. Ensure new tools and processes are adopted, governed, documented, and sustained across the team. Lead and Develop the Actuarial Strategic Operations Team: Lead, coach, and develop a team of financial operations and Actuarial professionals responsible for complex modeling, analysis, business partnership, and executive decision support. Set clear priorities and performance expectations, allocate work based on business impact and capacity, provide regular feedback and development opportunities, address performance concerns, and build the capabilities needed to support Clover’s evolving Medicare Advantage strategy. Success in this role looks like: In your first 90 days You will build strong cross-functional partnerships with business leaders to understand priorities, align on objectives, and establish the Command Center as a trusted strategic partner. You will establish the Command Center reporting framework by defining key performance indicators, leading and lagging metrics, and a consistent reporting cadence across functional areas. You will develop executive dashboards and scorecards that provide timely visibility into initiative performance, financial impact, and execution risks. You will assess team strengths, development needs, workload, and capacity, and establish clear roles, priorities, performance expectations, and operating rhythms. You will establish regular 1:1s, team forums, quality reviews, and development plans that support accountability and team growth. You will clarify how work is allocated across the Command Center and establish standards for financial analysis, modeling, executive reporting, and AI-enabled workflows. After 6 months You will lead executive operating reviews by delivering clear, data-driven insights on initiative performance, financial impact, emerging risks, and opportunities to senior leadership. You will implement a proactive risk monitoring framework that leverages leading indicators to identify execution gaps early and recommend timely mitigation strategies. You will establish yourself as a trusted strategic partner by providing actionable financial and operational insights that support executive decision-making, enterprise prioritization, and business planning. You will build a high-performing team that consistently delivers rigorous, timely, and actionable financial and operational insights. You will establish clear performance management and development practices, including measurable goals, regular feedback, and defined growth opportunities. You will demonstrate effective delegation and capacity planning across a portfolio of enterprise priorities, adjusting resources as business needs evolve. Future success in this role includes: Influence enterprise prioritization by providing data-driven insights that inform strategic investment decisions and resource allocation across the Medicare Advantage business. Drive automation and reporting excellence by continuously improving reporting processes, enhancing data quality, and increasing the efficiency and scalability of the Command Center operating model. Establish the Command Center as the enterprise source of truth for initiative performance, execution monitoring, and financial insights that support executive decision-making. Develop a sustainable Command Center talent model with clear roles, strong succession coverage, and the capabilities needed to support Clover’s evolving Medicare Advantage strategy. Create a culture of ownership, analytical excellence, constructive challenge, and continuous improvement across the team. Build team credibility with senior leaders by ensuring consistent quality, sound judgment, and measurable impact across enterprise decisions and initiatives. You will love this role if: You enjoy solving complex and ambiguous business challenges through data-driven analysis, AI-enabled exploration, and strategic problem solving. You are energized by influencing business strategy through financial insights, rapid experimentation, and actionable recommendations powered by modern analytical and AI tools. You thrive in highly collaborative environments, partnering across executive leadership and cross-functional teams to solve enterprise challenges and adopt new ways of working. You enjoy building new capabilities, AI-enabled workflows, and scalable operating models that improve organizational performance and create lasting business value. You should get in touch if: You are an Associate or Fellow of the Society of Actuaries and a Member of the American Academy of Actuaries. You have experience: 7-10 years of progressive experience in actuarial, healthcare finance, population health, analytics, consulting, strategy, or operations, with demonstrated success leading cross-functional initiatives and driving organizational change. Experience applying AI to improve analytical workflows, operational efficiency, or business decision-making is strongly preferred. You have industry Knowledge: Strong understanding of Medicare Advantage economics, including medical cost trends, utilization management, risk adjustment, provider reimbursement, or value-based care. title: Principal Embedded Systems Security Engineer at true
full_text: Space is a warfighting domain. True Anomaly seeks those with the talent and ambition to build the technology that secures it. OUR MISSION True Anomaly delivers decisive capabilities for space superiority. We build autonomous spacecraft, advanced payloads, mission software, and space-based interceptors — enabling the U.S. and its Allies to secure the space environment and counter threats from the ultimate high ground. OUR VALUES Be the offset. We create asymmetric advantages with creativity and ingenuity. What would it take? We challenge assumptions to deliver ambitious results. It’s the people. Our team is our competitive advantage and we are better together. YOUR MISSION Embedded systems security for space operations poses unique challenges: remote systems that must operate in adversarial RF environments, resource- constrained hardware, and trade-offs between security and performance in real-time systems. As our Principal Embedded Systems Security Engineer, you’ll own the security of our spacecraft, radio systems, and hardware platforms. You’ll build security platforms and foundational services that enable our hardware and software teams to develop secure embedded systems by default. This role demands deep security expertise and the rigor that comes from engineering systems that cannot fail. As part of the Platform Security team, you’ll work hands-on across C++ flight software, embedded C firmware within microcontrollers and radiation-hardened SoCs, FPGA designs, and real-time operating systems. Your work will impact the spacecraft’s critical subsystems, from flight computer through command and control, RF, and payload. If you’ve secured systems where failure means loss of life or national security impact, you’ll understand the constraints and rigor required here. This is a hands-on technical leadership role combining deep hardware security expertise with strong software engineering skills. You will write production code and build the tooling, test frameworks, and security validation platforms that harden our embedded systems at scale. You’ll tackle novel security challenges that don’t have an established playbook as we aim to set the standard for space-based security. In our AI-native environment, you’ll use AI to accelerate your work and help solve the hard problems of embedded systems security. This position requires the ability to obtain and maintain a security clearance. Responsibilities Own the security architecture, threat modeling, and defensive controls for our spacecraft platform. This spans the flight computer, subsystem firmware, FPGA gateware, cryptographic implementations, and secure boot. Architect and build the security platforms, tooling, and foundational services that make secure-by-default the standard across flight software, firmware, and hardware configuration. Design and implement PKI for resource-constrained spacecraft, covering device authentication, firmware signing and verification, secure boot, lifecycle management, and secure key storage. Architect cryptographic and security implementations to meet stringent government standards, including FIPS 140-3, CNSA 2.0, and CCSDS Space Data Link Security (SDLS), and drive the migration to post-quantum cryptography across the platform. Secure the flight software build and deployment pipeline by hardening the tooling itself and protecting the supply-chain integrity of build outputs, dependencies, and third-party components. Secure our test environments against supply-chain attacks while keeping them representative of the flight security posture, so we can exercise on the ground the controls used to protect the spacecraft in orbit. Lead security assessments and penetration testing against our spacecraft, RF systems, and test environments. Drive the adoption of secure design practices across the organization, partnering with flight software, hardware, and test engineering teams to embed security into the full development and validation lifecycle. Tackle novel security challenges in space-based systems where established solutions don’t exist, and stay ahead of emerging embedded and RF threats to proactively harden our systems. Use AI to move faster — accelerating development, analyzing security data, and closing technical knowledge gaps. Required Qualifications Active security clearance, or the ability to obtain and maintain one. Deep, hands-on expertise in embedded, hardware, and firmware security — including hardware attack surfaces, side-channel and fault-injection attacks, firmware security, secure boot, and hardware security modules (HSMs). Strong software development skills in C and C++, plus solid engineering fundamentals (data structures, algorithms, API design, and debugging production systems) and comfort working across multiple languages and at low levels (assembly, firmware). Proven track record of building production security platforms, tooling, and foundational services used by hardware and embedded engineering teams. Deep, expert-level PKI knowledge with hands-on experience designing and operating PKI for embedded and resource-constrained systems —certificate-based device authentication, firmware signing certificate chains, secure boot PKI hierarchies, certificate provisioning and rotation for constrained devices (where rotation isn’t trivial, e.g., spacecraft in orbit), secure key storage, and HSM integration. Expert-level applied cryptography: implementing and reasoning about cryptographic systems to stringent government standards (FIPS 140-3, and familiarity with CNSA 2.0 and CCSDS SDLS), and experience with the practical challenges of post-quantum cryptography migration. Strong familiarity with common NIST publications (e.g., the 800-series). Experience applying security testing methodologies for hardware and firmware, and building the tooling and frameworks to automate that testing at scale across engineering teams. Demonstrated principal-level impact: setting security strategy and technical direction across an organization, independently identifying and prioritizing the risks that matter most, driving hardening initiatives end to end, raising the security bar and mentoring other engineers, thriving on ambiguous and novel problems, and influencing and aligning teams without direct authority. Preferred Qualifications Hands-on experience taking cryptographic modules through formal FIPS validation (CMVP), beyond implementing to the standard. Experience with real-time or safety-critical embedded systems — timing constraints, deterministic execution, interrupt handling, and the security implications of hard real-time requirements. Background in a regulated or high-assurance domain: aerospace, defense, avionics, medical devices, or industrial control systems. Hardware reverse engineering, firmware analysis, and cryptographic implementation experience. FPGA/VHDL security and RF/radio security. HIL/SIL test infrastructure and embedded Linux environments. Supply-chain security experience and a track record of hardening build pipelines for embedded/firmware systems. Cross-domain thinking that connects hardware security requirements to cloud infrastructure, network security, and system architecture. Evidence of practical, hands-on impact — published CVEs, security research or publications, conference talks, open-source contributions, or relevant projects Base Salary: $225,000-$330,000 Equity + Benefits including Health, Dental, Vision, HRA/HSA options, PTO and paid holidays, 401K, Parental Leave Your actual level and base salary will be determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on the following considerations: job-related knowledge and skills, education, location, and experience. title: Content Manager (Remote, £33-38k) at Ellipsis®
full_text: Ellipsis is emerging as a market leader in “GEO” for B2B technology companies. This is a high-impact, varied role in a fast-moving and ambitious agency. The transition to AI search has put a lot of the SEO industry on the back foot. Ellipsis has always been consultative/strategic in our approach; we started building AI search products in 2021 on GPT-2, and thus this has been a time for us to thrive. Today, we think we have a better understanding of AI search than almost anyone else. We have both the tracking product (built in-house), the data (~25 million AI answers for analysis, with more tracked weekly), and the execution end-to-end from strategy, to writing, to in-house design, to optimization, and performance reporting. As our newest Content Manager, you will be the engineer who ensures the content production machine runs optimally. You’ll be the primary point of contact and own end-to-end delivery of content deliverables for your own portfolio of clients. This means ultimate responsibility for ensuring that every piece of content is delivered on time, on brief, and meets our high bar for quality. We have an increasingly varied (and growing) portfolio of clients and are looking for an experienced project manager to maintain – and improve upon – our high delivery standards. It is an exciting time to join us. What you’ll do The Content Manager role is varied, fast-paced, and requires a high level of organizational capability. You’ll be responsible for a mixture of big-picture client, project and account management (~70% of your time) and in-the-weeds production work (~30% of your time), giving you a uniquely rounded perspective on each of your client accounts. The heart of the role is in client and project management – you’ll be the main point of contact for a portfolio of clients, and shoulder much of the responsibility for managing these client relationships, keeping delivery on track, and ensuring quality remains high. Excellent written and verbal communication skills are central to being an effective Content Manager. You’ll regularly communicate directly with clients via Slack, email, and Trello, and lead fortnightly or monthly check-in meetings, often with multiple stakeholders. You’ll need to be confident preparing for these, presenting to clients, and handling questions or concerns appropriately live on calls. Organization, critical thinking, and an eye for detail are all equally critical. Our Content Managers are ultimately responsible for ensuring that every deliverable for each of their clients is delivered on time, does its intended job, and measures up to both our high internal standards and individual client requirements: On time We produce a high volume of content at Ellipsis, and we do so quickly! You’ll need to be adept at prioritizing different task types across your client portfolio, coordinating with our in-house Writing and Strategy teams to ensure dependencies are met when scheduling tasks, and proactive in reorganising your (and others’) workloads according to internal and external factors. You’ll be relentless in driving work forward and comfortable with chasing both clients and internal team members to keep delivery on track. On brief As a Content Manager, you’ll hold a holistic view of your client accounts. You’ll understand your clients’ priorities and goals, how our content strategy ties into them, and how each deliverable feeds into that strategy. You’ll have ultimate responsibility for understanding the intended job of each piece of content, properly briefing the Writing team before they start work, and ensuring that each finished article or page meets the requirements of the brief before it goes to the client. In practice, this means you’ll: Work closely with our Strategy team to ensure our recommended programme of work matches the client’s needs. Produce high-quality content outlines (briefs) for the writing team before they start work. Own the final quality check of each content piece prior to delivery. Up to standard We take content quality very seriously at Ellipsis. As a Content Manager, the buck stops with you on quality – you’ll need to maintain meticulous editorial standards across your clients’ content, and ensure that each piece: Is optimized according to our (constantly evolving) AI optimization thesis. Meets individual client voice, messaging, and style guidelines. Is user-friendly and visually engaging when published on the client’s site. You’ll need to be obsessive with keeping client requirements updated internally, abreast of the latest changes to our optimization thesis, and confident speaking up or pushing back when a piece of content needs more work. At Ellipsis, we pride ourselves on continuous improvement. As a Content Manager, you’ll be right at the heart of many of our core processes, and will have the opportunity to have a significant impact in shaping and improving our workflows as we continue to grow and develop the team. If you’re obsessed with – and skilled in – keeping things organized, improving efficiency, and solving problems, this could be a dream role for you. We’re looking for a highly organized project manager, adept at managing both client and internal relationships. We’d expect at least 3-4 years of experience in a project management, client/account management, or similar role. Beyond this, a meticulous eye for quality, an ability to identify problems or blockers, and a proactive approach to solving them are hard requirements. You’ll need to be confident in getting up to speed fast on unfamiliar B2B and SaaS topics and ensuring that each piece of content we ship is compelling, user-friendly, and optimized for AI and legacy search. A working understanding of GEO would be an advantage, but what we’re really looking for is somebody with an eagerness to learn and the ability to do so quickly. Strong critical thinking is a must-have at Ellipsis! If a deliverable doesn’t appear to align with client goals, or a completed article doesn’t match the brief, you’ll need to be confident in calling it out. We are looking for candidates who can spot gaps or friction within our current processes and systems, and help drive forward improvements. As a 100% remote team, we carefully balance collaboration with an environment that enables everyone to do their best work. You’ll need to be confident in communicating with the team through Basecamp (our project management software) and Google Meet, and with clients through Slack, Email, and video calls. The majority of the team is located in Europe, and we have clients all over the world. You’ll thus be expected to regularly attend meetings between 9am–5pm GMT, with occasional calls outside these times. Beyond the above, the ideal candidate will be able to demonstrate the following soft skills: Receptive to feedback with no ego and solutions-oriented: You can take a constructive critique, act on it, and get better. At Ellipsis, continuous improvement is more important than being right. High level of self-awareness, a “people person”: You’ll be dealing with clients and members of the team on a daily basis, so this is an integral part of the role. Self-driven work ethic: You need to be self-motivated, proactive, and see projects through to completion. Compensation This is a full-time, 100% remote role. You’ll be a full team member, and involved in our team projects, work, and meetups. Competitive salary with pension benchmarked to UK rates and based on experience. £33-38k/year salary, depending on experience. 28 days of paid holiday An additional 1 paid holiday day a year with each year of tenure, up to a maximum of 5 additional days. 4-day work week, once a month. Genuinely flexible working. Regular team retreats (~1 per year); last was Istanbul, previously in Edinburgh, Oxford, Madrid, and Budapest. Time and budget for learning and development. Enhanced maternity/paternity leave, and sick pay. Application process It’s important we find the best candidate for this position, and our selection process will reflect this. You’ll be required to attend at least three interviews (by video call) and carry out a (paid) freelance project with us before we make an employment offer. Much of our company Wiki is externally accessible, and you’re encouraged to read through this before applying. We have a very useful guide to our interview process available here. This tells you what we’re looking for and reading this will significantly increase your chance of success! Please apply through Workable: https://apply.workable.com/getellipsis. We will decide who progresses to the next stage based on the form you submit, your cover letter, and your CV. Please give us a good reason to select you! Taking the time to research the role, what we’re looking for, what we do, and what you can do for us will increase your chance of success. Your cover letter is where you have the space to do this. Whilst we love technology and sit at the leading edge of its adoption (we automate hundreds of thousands of actions a month internally), we want to hear from you rather than from ChatGPT. The deadline for submission is the end of the day, on 30th September 2026. We’ll be in touch with all candidates following the close of applications. We do great work for clients and are building an ethical business that lets everyone do their best work. If you think you could be the next person to join our team, please apply!

title: QE Platform Engineer at OnePay
full_text: About OnePay OnePay is the consumer fintech trusted by millions of Americans to make money better. Our financial system is broken. High fees, low rates, and too few ways to actually grow your money. We’re fixing it. And we’re moving fast. We’re an all-in-one financial services platform that brings together banking, high-yield savings, credit cards, point-of-sale lending, investing, and crypto in one place. We also partner with employers, HCM providers, gig platforms, and others to deliver embedded financial services to millions of employees and frontline workers. We’re backed by Walmart, the world’s largest retailer, and Ribbit Capital, one of fintech’s most respected investors, giving us rare scale, distribution, and the opportunity to build something truly category-defining. But what really sets OnePay apart is how we move. Our customers don’t have time to wait… and neither do we. This place moves fast, and we’re looking for people who are: Ready to run Hungry and driven by urgency Exceptional at what they do, with low ego Comfortable operating in motion The Role As a QE Platform Engineer at OnePay, your work will directly shape how confidently every engineering team ships to production — building the test automation infrastructure that catches problems before they reach customers of a financial platform millions of people trust. You will: Design and own shared test automation frameworks used by engineering teams across web, mobile, and backend services Build and maintain test execution infrastructure that runs automated suites reliably at scale, including flaky-test detection and triage tooling Partner with engineering teams to raise test coverage and testing maturity, embedding quality practices into the development workflow rather than bolting them on afterward Develop tooling for test environment provisioning, test data management, and parallelized test execution to keep feedback loops fast Instrument and monitor test infrastructure health (pass rates, run times, flakiness) and drive down friction points that slow teams down Contribute to internal documentation and best practices that help other engineers write and maintain effective automated tests You Bring 5+ years of professional experience in test automation, QE engineering, or backend/platform engineering with a strong testing focus Deep experience designing and building test automation frameworks and tooling (e.g., Playwright, Selenium, Appium, Cypress) that other engineers build on Proficiency in TypeScript/Node.js or similar languages, with experience architecting test frameworks rather than just writing test cases Experience with cloud-native infrastructure (Kubernetes, AWS) and containerized test environments Familiarity with testing across the stack — API/integration testing, end-to-end testing for web and mobile (e.g., React Native) Strong communication and collaboration skills, able to influence testing practices across multiple engineering teams Drive and proactivity - everyone here is a builder and executor Tools We Use We use Node and TypeScript on the server, leveraging the NestJS framework within a microservice-oriented architecture running on Kubernetes and AWS. On the client side, we build and ship product features for iOS, Android, and web platforms using React Native. We also embrace AI-assisted development, so engineers have their choice of Claude Code or Cursor to fit their workflow. While you don’t need experience with our exact stack, familiarity with modern software engineering practices will help you ramp up quickly. Most candidates go through: AI-assisted initial screen Interview with Talent Partner Technical or Hiring Manager Interview Team Interview Executive Interview Offer! Equal Employment Opportunity To build technology and products that are used and loved by people and solve real-world problems, we need to build a team with many different perspectives and experiences. We are an equal opportunity employer. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status. We encourage candidates from all backgrounds to apply. Applicants in need of special assistance or accommodation during the interview process or in accessing our website may contact us at talent@onepay.com.

title: NetSuite Systems Engineer at DoiT
full_text: Location As a Financial Systems Engineer, you will be part of Business Systems Engineering, a group of several teams that builds and runs the systems the company operates on. This role is based remotely in the United States (Eastern time zone), the UK, or Ireland. Who We Are DoiT is a global technology company that works with cloud-driven organizations to leverage the cloud to drive business growth and innovation. We combine data, technology, and human expertise to ensure our customers are operating in a well-architected and scalable state - from planning to production. Delivering DoiT Cloud Intelligence, the only solution that integrates advanced technology with human intelligence, we help our customers solve complex multi-cloud problems and drive efficiency. With decades of multicloud experience, we have specializations in Kubernetes, GenAI, CloudOps, and more. An award-winning strategic partner of AWS, Google Cloud, Microsoft Azure and Ingram Micro, we work alongside more than 4,000 customers worldwide. The Opportunity We are modernizing how we run our financial systems and bringing this work in-house, and we’re looking for a Financial Systems Engineer to own it. You will own our financial systems - NetSuite today, with FloQast and Ramp coming online - as an engineer, not just an administrator. What sets this role apart is mindset. You are the kind of person who is averse to doing the same manual task twice and instinctively looks for ways to automate it away. You will own the configuration and business logic of the financial systems, keeping each one doing what it does best, and partner with our internal engineering team on cross-system integration rather than wiring it together by hand. This is a high-ownership role serving Finance and Accounting directly. You will be their dedicated systems partner - someone who knows the platforms deeply, is invested in making them better, and treats reducing manual, error-prone work as the core of the job rather than something to do on the side. Reporting to the Manager of Enterprise Systems, you will have real room to shape how finance operations run as the company scales Responsibilities Own and administer our core financial systems - NetSuite today, with FloQast and Ramp coming online - including configuration, business logic, and day-to-day system health. Identify manual, recurring, or error-prone finance operations (month-end close, reconciliations, reporting, procure-to-pay) and reduce or remove them through automation, choosing the simplest effective approach and partnering with engineering for heavier builds. Serve as the business-logic and data expert for the finance domain, partnering with engineering to define and maintain the rules and canonical definitions the systems rely on. Build cross-system integrations on a central, version-controlled, observable integration platform in partnership with engineering, rather than as one-off scripts buried inside individual tools. Act as the dedicated systems partner to Finance and Accounting: translate their needs into system capability, own those working relationships, and serve as the technical owner for financial-vendor onboarding, configuration, and administration. Use modern AI tooling to draft automations and accelerate routine system work, amplifying your output rather than adding manual effort. Qualifications 3-6 years administering a financial or ERP system, with hands-on NetSuite administration required, including: configuration, customization, user access, roles, permissions, and workflows; core modules such as General Ledger, Advanced Revenue Management, Accounts, and subsidiary / multi-location structures; designing and implementing custom records, fields, and automations; building SuiteFlow automations in response to changing business needs; managing the NetSuite integration ecosystem. A working understanding of core finance and accounting processes: month-end close, reconciliation, accounts payable / procure-to-pay, and revenue. A strong drive to eliminate repetitive manual work, with a demonstrated track record of automating it (e.g. scripting, saved searches, workflow automation, or low-code/iPaaS tools). Sound judgment about where logic belongs - what should be system configuration, what should be a cross-system integration, and which system is the source of truth for a given piece of data. Comfort with at least one of SuiteScript, SQL, general scripting, or API-based automation, and the ability to read and reason about integrations even when engineering builds them. Strong collaboration and communication across both finance and engineering teams, with the ability to translate between them. Fluent English; knowledge of any other language is an advantage. Bonus Points: FloQast and/or Ramp administration experience. Experience working against a central integration platform or in an event-driven environment. Comfort using AI coding and automation tools in day-to-day work. Depth in SuiteScript (1.0 / 2.0), RESTlets, or NetSuite web services. Are you a Do’er? Be your truest self. Work on your terms. Make a difference. We are home to a global team of incredible talent who work remotely and have the flexibility to have a schedule that balances your work and home life. We embrace and support leveling up your skills professionally and personally. What does being a Do’er mean? We’re all about being entrepreneurial, pursuing knowledge, and having fun! Click here to learn more about our core values. Sounds too good to be true? Check out our Glassdoor Page. We thought so too, but we’re here and happy we hit that ‘apply’ button. Full-time employee benefits include: Unlimited Vacation Flexible Working Options Health Insurance Parental Leave Employee Stock Option Plan Home Office Allowance Professional Development Stipend Peer Recognition Program Many Do’ers, One Team DoiT unites as Many Do’ers, One Team , where diversity is more than a goal—it’s our strength. We actively cultivate an inclusive, equitable workplace, recognizing that each unique perspective enhances our innovation. By celebrating differences, we create an environment where every individual feels valued, contributing to our collective success. #LI-Remote

title: Payroll Specialist at Sona (getsona.com)
full_text: Frontline work keeps the world running. Restaurants, hospitals, schools, nurseries, airlines, stores, emergency services. Together they employ 80% of the global workforce, over 3 billion people, and they’re among the hardest businesses anywhere to run. By-the-minute scheduling, HR and payroll make them far more operationally complex than the average office, yet just 1% of venture funding has ever gone to software built for them. Rising costs, wage increases, labour shortages and tighter regulation have made fixing that urgent. Sona is the AI-native workforce management platform for frontline organisations, with agents that match staffing to real demand and take the admin load off managers. That’s a $500bn+ market the software industry has mostly walked past. We’ve raised over $100M from N47, Felicis, Gradient and Northzone, signed more than 100 enterprise customers across the UK and US, and opened offices in London, New York, Austin and Lisbon. More on working at Sona here. About the Role We’re hiring a Payroll Specialist to join Sona’s payroll bureau, taking hands-on ownership of UK payroll processing for a portfolio of our customers. Our bureau is growing fast. We’re moving from around 15,000 payslips a month to roughly 22,000 by the start of Q4, driven by new customer go-lives in hospitality and care. That means the pace of the role is genuinely high, and we’re hiring ahead of that curve rather than catching up after the fact. Day to day, you’ll manage a portfolio of standard and mid-complexity clients across multiple pay frequencies: statutory payments, pension auto-enrolment, HMRC filings and payroll journal reconciliation. You’ll also handle client queries through our support desk, working to fast turnaround times. Your work is checked by a Senior Payroll Specialist before it reaches clients, as part of our standard quality process. This isn’t a conventional bureau role. Sona is a startup and the payroll team is still building its own processes and tools, so there’s genuine room to shape how things work and to grow as the bureau scales. You’ll be working on a product in a sector most software has ignored, and once you’re through probation we support CIPP study through the apprenticeship levy. Responsibilities Own end-to-end UK payroll processing for a portfolio of Sona customers across multiple pay frequencies, covering standard and mid-complexity clients Manage payroll queries through our support desk, giving clients fast, proactive updates and resolving within SLA Process statutory payments, court orders, standard holiday pay calculations, Alabaster reviews and NMW checks for your own portfolio Handle workplace pension auto-enrolment, contributions, reconciliations and submissions, flagging any miscalculated contributions for investigation Upload, reconcile and submit payments across BACS, Faster Payments and SEPA, and manage payroll journal uploads and reconciliations Manage HMRC filings (FPS, EPS) and year-end processing for your portfolio, escalating disputed or mis-allocated PAYE cases to your Senior or the Payroll Manager Build strong working relationships with clients, including attending client meetings when needed, and flag product bugs to Engineering as you spot them Spot and flag process gaps or improvements within your own portfolio, and support Payroll Assistants and Senior Payroll Specialists with day-to-day queries Requirements 2+ years hands-on experience processing multiple UK payrolls independently Experience within a bureau or outsourced payroll environment is a bonus Good working knowledge of UK payroll and tax compliance, including tax calculations and filing and payment requirements Confident managing a busy queue of support tickets, with strong organisational skills and clear written and verbal communication Comfortable in Excel (VLOOKUPs, pivot tables, concatenation) and Google Suite Methodical and accurate under volume, and quick to flag issues rather than let them become problems Bonus: CIPP or equivalent qualification, exposure to Irish payroll (PAYE, PRSI, USC), or confidence using AI tools in your day-to-day work Benefits Salary: £35,000 - £45,000 Hybrid working - 2+ days/week in our London office (Soho) Share options 35 days annual leave (25 days standard plus 10 flexible public holiday days) Extra day of leave for every year of service Pension contributions matched up to 5% Comprehensive health insurance Enhanced parental leave & pay Salary sacrifice childcare scheme (Workplace Nursery) Annual all expenses paid team retreats The latest Macbook and equipment budget for your home office Professional development budget Unlimited free books Note: this represents a typical benefits package for a UK-based, full-time employee. title: Senior Marketing Manager, ABM at Figure
full_text: About Figure Figure (NASDAQ: FIGR) is transforming capital markets through blockchain. We’re proving that blockchain isn’t just theory - it’s powering real products used by hundreds of thousands of consumers and institutions. By combining blockchain’s transparency and efficiency with AI-driven automation, we’ve reimagined how loans are originated, funded, and traded in secondary markets. From faster processing times to lower costs and reduced bias, our technology is helping borrowers, investors, and financial institutions achieve better outcomes. Together with our 170+ partners, we’ve originated over $22 billion in home equity loans (HELOCs) on our blockchain-native platform, making Figure the largest non-bank provider of home equity financing in the U.S. Figure’s ecosystem also includes YLDS, an SEC-registered yield-bearing stablecoin that operates as a tokenized money market fund, and several other products and platforms that are reshaping consumer finance and capital markets. We’re proud to be recognized as one of Forbes’ Most Innovative Fintech Startups in 2025 and Fast Company’s Most Innovative Companies in Finance and Personal Finance. About the Role We are looking for a dynamic, driven B2B marketing professional to own our Account-Based Marketing (ABM) and cold outbound initiatives. In this role, you will act as the bridge between marketing (content, events), partnerships and sales, driving the pipeline for our key segments: Independent Mortgage Banks / Servicers, Wholesale Brokers, SMBs, Home Improvement, Banks, and Credit Unions. You are an “outbound hacker” at heart, but one who knows how to build scalable systems, and coordinate with sales . You won’t be executing every channel yourself; instead, you will bring the data together, target the accounts, define the messaging, and hand those systems off to our strong channel marketing team to deploy. Take a hands-on approach to grading, tiering, and contact-mapping our core target segments. Identify key behavioral trigger points to launch highly impactful, “always-on” automated journeys. Tie everything together. You are ultimately responsible for defining what success looks like and tracking cross-channel performance to prove direct impact on meetings booked, SQLs, and pipeline generated. You will build reports in Salesforce to tell a clear story with data and diagnose CRM sync issues to convey solutions to our tech team. Build the targeting and messaging systems that power our ABM efforts for both cold outbounding and current prospects. Taking cold leads to warm leads to keeping the warm leads engaged throughout a longer sales cycle. Working in tandem with sales to discover key points in the sales prospecting cycle to pull accounts faster to onboarding. You will supply our highly capable channel teams with the exact data and messaging they need to execute direct mail, gifting, and LinkedIn campaigns effectively. While you won’t be writing all the content yourself, you will act as the final filter. You should have an opinion on whether messaging will resonate and be able to give direction if the output misses the mark. You will also build streamlined systems for deploying this content to the sales team. Partner closely with our Field Marketing Manager to identify the highest-impact events to reach our target accounts, supplying them with the targeted ABM data and tactics (pre- and post-event) to maximize our physical presence. What We Look For Proven experience in B2B marketing, specifically building Account-Based Marketing, Outbound, or Demand Generation engines. You don’t just “set it and forget it.” You love building automated workflows, you are constantly running A/B tests on messaging and targeting, and you use data to relentlessly optimize your approach. Hands-on experience with cold email and data platforms (e.g., Lemlist, Apollo, Clay, Outreach). You are comfortable working inside HubSpot and Salesforce. You don’t need to be a backend developer, but you know how the systems talk to each other, how to diagnose sync issues, and how to pull a reliable pipeline report. Experience in fintech or banking is a massive plus. Adhere to all company security policies and data handling procedures. Complete mandatory security awareness training within required timeframes. Promptly report any suspected security incidents or suspicious activity to the Security team. What Success Looks Like In 30 Days: Audit our current target account lists using Apollo and Clay, launch your first always-on cold email sequences, and familiarize yourself with our HubSpot/Salesforce reporting dashboards. In 60 Days: Build the data and messaging hand-off system for our channel managers to launch a coordinated ABM campaign. Establish a strong feedback loop with the sales team to review the quality of SQLs and meetings being booked, and begin running your first structured A/B tests on outbound messaging. In 90 Days: Have a fully functioning outbound engine and event-support motion running. You will be able to clearly point to the SQLs and pipeline generated by your systems and share data-backed optimization plans for the next quarter. If you love living in data enrichment tools, building multi-channel systems, obsessing over A/B testing, and have a sharp eye for what makes B2B messaging convert, this role is for you. title: Senior DevOps Cloud Engineer (Hybrid - Indianapolis or Dallas) at Resultant
full_text: Company Description Resultant is a modern consulting firm with a radically different approach to solving problems. We don’t solve problems for our clients. We solve problems with them. Through outcomes driven by data analytics, technology solutions, digital transformation, and beyond, our team works with clients in both the public and private sectors to solve their most complex challenges. We start by learning as much as we can about who they are, how they work, and what they’re striving for so we can feel their problems as our own. Partnering with our clients means their desired outcomes are always top of mind, their challenges and strengths guiding our efforts. We build client-focused relationships before we build unique solutions that blaze past expectations. Originally founded in Indianapolis as KSM Consulting in 2008, Resultant now employs more than 350 team members who operate from offices around the United States including Indianapolis and Fort Wayne, Indiana; Columbus, Ohio; Lansing, Michigan; Denver, Colorado; Dallas, Texas and Atlanta, Georgia. We’re Resultant. Clients partner with us to see a difference. People join us to make one. Job Description About the Role We are looking for a Senior Cloud Engineer to serve as the senior-most technical authority for how we design, build, and operate infrastructure across AWS, Google Cloud, and Azure. This is a hands-on, infrastructure-focused role for an engineer who has spent more than a decade in production environments and now sets the standards, patterns, and reference architectures that entire teams build on. You will own the hardest architecture decisions, act as the final technical escalation point, and multiply the impact of every engineer around you. You will work across internal platforms and client-facing engagements, shaping solutions from pre-sales through production. This is a principal-level individual contributor role and design authority. Your leverage comes from the standards you set, the accelerators you build, and the technical direction you drive across the practice, not from managing people. Key Responsibilities Technical authority. Act as the design authority for multi-cloud infrastructure across AWS, Google Cloud, and Azure. Own the hardest architecture decisions and serve as the final escalation point for production-critical problems across engagements. Standards and reference architectures. Define the firm-wide standards, patterns, and reference architectures for landing zones, networking, identity, and workload platforms that every team builds on. Set account, subscription, and project structure, environment separation, and identity boundaries as defaults. Infrastructure as Code. Own the IaC standard for the practice. Build the reusable, modular Terraform and the module library that other engineers adopt by default, and govern state, versioning, and drift at scale. Container platforms. Set the standard for running Kubernetes in production (EKS, GKE, AKS), including networking, autoscaling, workload isolation, and day-2 operations. Own container registries and artifact promotion (ECR, ACR, Artifact Registry) and golden image pipelines (cloud-init, image bake) for consistent, hardened builds. Solutioning and pre-sales. Shape proposals and estimates, lead technical discovery, and represent the firm as the senior cloud voice in client and executive conversations. Delivery automation. Build and harden CI/CD pipelines and deployment automation that move code to production safely and repeatably. Reliability. Establish observability, SLOs, and incident response practices. Lead root cause analysis and drive permanent fixes rather than repeated firefighting. Security and compliance. Define the cloud security and compliance posture: identity and least-privilege access, secrets management, network segmentation, encryption, and policy as code. Cost and efficiency. Drive cost visibility and optimization (FinOps) across accounts, projects, and clouds. Leadership and mentorship. Raise the technical bar across the practice. Mentor and grow senior engineers, shape the hiring bar, and lead design reviews. Accelerators. Build the accelerators and reference implementations that cut delivery time and raise quality across every engagement. Qualifications Must Have 12+ years in cloud infrastructure, DevOps, or platform engineering, with deep production ownership and a record of setting technical direction. Deep, hands-on expertise across all three of AWS, Google Cloud, and Azure, or mastery of two with strong production experience in the third. Expert-level Infrastructure as Code, especially Terraform, with patterns and module libraries you have personally established as the standard across multiple teams. Production Kubernetes experience (EKS, GKE, or AKS), including day-2 operations and troubleshooting. Strong CI/CD design experience (GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Azure DevOps, Jenkins, or similar). Advanced scripting and automation in Python, Bash, and/or PowerShell. Deep networking fundamentals across clouds: VPC and VNet design, DNS, load balancing, hybrid connectivity, and private-by-default access patterns (PrivateLink, Private Service Connect, Shared VPC, and multi-account or multi-project connectivity). Strong grounding in cloud security and identity (IAM, RBAC, secrets management, encryption).
