Identify adoption risks and operational-change requirements early, then work directly with customer champions and users to establish a durable new workflow. Measure whether the implementation is producing the intended business result and adjust the system or process based on evidence. Turn repeated customer needs and field lessons into product direction, implementation playbooks, reusable platform capabilities, and expansion opportunities. Build trusted relationships with customer executives, operators, finance teams, and technical stakeholders through clarity, judgment, and follow-through. Qualifications At least 3 years of experience owning implementations, analytical or operational programs, customer delivery, or similarly ambiguous cross-functional work. We care more about repeated evidence of ownership and learning velocity than an exact tenure threshold. Experience carrying an important initiative from discovery and planning through implementation, adoption, and results. Strong analytical fluency and willingness to work directly with data and models using tools such as SQL, spreadsheets, BI platforms, workflow automation, and AI-assisted analysis. Ability to translate between business and technical teams and turn an ambiguous problem into a sequence of concrete decisions and deliverables. Strong customer judgment: you build trust, communicate tradeoffs clearly, handle difficult moments constructively, and create forward motion. High agency in an early-stage environment: you create structure where little exists, surface risks before they become escalations, and do the hands-on work necessary to keep delivery moving. Willingness and interest in traveling approximately 10–20% for customer meetings and team sessions in Bellevue, Washington. This travel is an expected part of the role. Strong candidates may come from implementation or professional services, solutions consulting, technical customer success, analytics or data consulting, business or strategy operations, finance systems, FP&A, enterprise planning, or other backgrounds that combine analytical depth with delivery ownership. Helpful, but not required Experience with finance, accounting, FP&A, enterprise planning, ERP, or operational analytics. Experience implementing AI-enabled applications, agents, decision systems, or workflow automation in a real business process. Experience in a startup, consultancy, or lean internal team where responsibilities were broader than the title. Experience working closely with engineers or data scientists and making good technical tradeoffs without being the primary engineer. Working familiarity with Python and relational databases. Why Join Now Own meaningful customer and business outcomes. Help customers establish new AI-enabled operating processes. Work directly with the people building the product and turn field learning into product direction. Operate with high autonomy and little organizational distance between identifying a problem and fixing it. Grow quickly through broad customer, analytical, product, and operating responsibility. Participate meaningfully in the value you help create through equity. title: Lead Product Manager, Customer Portal
full_text: About Customer Portal Customer Portal exists to make Veriff's product sell itself. The Portal serves two purposes. It allows our customers to operate Veriff products — setting up and configuring products, consulting verification session details, reporting issues. And it is a privileged surface for customers to discover, try, buy and expand through a seamless self-serve experience, connecting product usage, onboarding and growth in one place. It unites forces with GTM to automate acquisition, upsell, cross-sell and retention, with end-to-end ownership of the customer persona. The area is evolving fast. What began as a self-serve growth surface (Station) is becoming the customer-facing window into Veriff's accuracy and fraud advantage for our largest enterprise customers. The shape of this role This is an IC-first leadership role, and the first genuine step into product leadership — distinct from a strong senior IC. At first you will lead through craft, authority and influence. You own the strategy, discovery, roadmap and delivery for your product area. As you refine the strategic themes for this large product, we expect you to propose the team configuration needed to support our growth and company objectives. That will move you progressively from IC to manager, while retaining hands-on ownership of at least one part of the Customer Portal area in the mid-term. We will deliberately assess for both the IC craft bar and the latent management capability, because the role is designed to traverse the line. What you will do Own the product strategy and roadmap for the Customer Portal area, tied explicitly to Veriff's commercial model and revenue drivers. Run disciplined, continuous discovery with customers, and translate it into well-defined problem statements and a sequenced roadmap. Make transparent prioritisation and trade-off calls across product ambition, technical sustainability and business urgency — especially where capability gaps mean we cannot do everything at once. Define success metrics before building, and hold the team accountable to outcomes, not output. Partner as a credible peer to Engineering, GTM, Fraud Ops and Design. Be the connective tissue that turns internal expertise into a customer-facing product. Own launch as a discipline from the start — internal platform releases and external GTM — not a milestone at the end. Set and uphold the product-craft bar. Mentor PMs and, in time, build and lead the team. Champion AI internally, implementing new best practices for faster product discovery and delivery. Who you are You are a product leader who has earned authority through the quality of your thinking rather than a title. You have owned a product area end-to-end From strategy through discovery, delivery and launch. You are equally comfortable in the messy front end of a problem and in the discipline of shipping. You are looking for the step where your impact starts to come through others, and you are excited that this role begins as an individual leader and grows into managing a team — not the other way around. You think commercially You instinctively connect what you build to how the business grows, and you explain the “why” behind a product bet in terms of revenue, retention and customer trust, not just features and flows. You run discovery as a continuous discipline You get close to customers, including demanding enterprise accounts, and you can tell the difference between what they ask for and what they actually need. You turn that into sharp problem statements and a phased roadmap where every step delivers a real customer outcome. You prioritise ruthlessly and transparently When there are more good ideas than capacity, you make the hard calls about what not to do, and you can articulate the reasoning. You define success before you build. When something goes wrong, you own it without deflection and change how you work as a result. You lead through influence, not authority You build credibility with engineering, go-to-market, design and operations partners as a genuine peer, and you reach good decisions with people who do not report to you. You stay calm under uncertainty, create space for views that differ from your own, and commit gracefully once a call is made. You raise the people around you You set a high craft bar through your own work, share your thinking generously and give specific, useful feedback. You are motivated by building and leading a team over time, with a realistic understanding that management is a different job — one focused on developing people and multiplying impact, not doing all the work yourself. You stay current on your craft You take pride in tracking how product management is evolving, and you consistently find time to experiment and fold what works into your practice. Why Veriff? We are the preferred identity verification platform partner for the world’s most innovative growth-driven organizations helping conveniently verify and safeguard users anywhere in the world. We support the broadest number of identity documents from nearly every country and territory in the world - and this is continually increasing! With a diverse team in the United States, United Kingdom, Spain, and Estonia, as well as robust backing and funding from investors including Accel, Alkeon, IVP, Tiger Capital, and Y Combinator, we’re dedicated to helping businesses and individuals build a safer and more secure world. We strive to be the benchmark for trust online, and we take pride in being a positive force.When you join Team Veriff, we offer you the opportunity to have a real impact and advance your career whilst looking after you along the way with a range of benefits designed with you in mind. Some of our favourites include... Flexibility to work from home Stock options that ensure your share in our success Extra recharge days on top of your annual vacation Extensive medical, dental, and vision insurance to ensure you’re feeling great physically and mentally Learning and Development & Health and Sports budget that you are free to tailor to your own needs Four weeks of fully paid sabbatical leave after reaching your 5th work anniversary We are an Equal Opportunities employer committed to a diverse and representative team. Different opinions, perspectives, and personalities push us forward. We want to hear from people who are passionate about their work and align with our values. Regardless of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, or disability. We also know the confidence gap and imposter syndrome can get in the way of meeting spectacular candidates - so rest assured, whoever you are, we want to hear from you! title: Fractional RevOps / GTM Engineer (Part-Time, Contract)
full_text: Anagram is the ultimate insurance billing platform for eye care providers. Combining instant eligibility and benefit verifications, patient responsibility calculation, claims management, payment posting, and more, Anagram's all-in-one revenue cycle management solution is designed to save providers time and money, and free doctors to deliver the best care for their patients. Our mission is to simplify insurance, and it's working: over 2,000 eye care professionals rely on Anagram to manage their insurance billing. Founded in 2014, Anagram is the largest and fastest-growing insurance billing platform for eye care providers in America and processes hundreds of millions of dollars each year. About the Role We're looking for a hands-on RevOps/GTM engineer to own the revenue systems layer across a genuinely messy and interesting go-to-market. You'll design and maintain the pipes connecting CRM, billing, warehouse, and analytics, and wire AI into the workflows in between. You'll work directly with revenue leadership and have wide latitude in how things get built. Why This Role Is Harder Than It Sounds The account hierarchy is real. Our market spans solo practices, multi-location companies, roll-up brands, and PE platforms. The HubSpot company object has to do quadruple duty — PE firm → brand → company → location — with clean parent-child associations, dedup logic that respects the hierarchy, and reporting that rolls up correctly at every level. Four GTM motions run in parallel. SMB, mid-market, enterprise, and partner led — each needs its own routing, lifecycle logic, handoffs, and funnel reporting, without forking the CRM into four incompatible systems. Three products, three pricing models. Subscription, usage-based, and percentage-of-collections billing all flow through the same revenue stack. Normalizing these into coherent ARR/NRR, cohort, and revenue reporting is a core design problem, not an afterthought. About You You're a hands-on RevOps/GTM engineer with a builder profile. Strong SQL from scratch. You know when a Zap is enough and when it's time to write code. Self-directed; comfortable operating fractionally with async communication and minimal oversight. What We're Looking For Must-Haves 4+ years in RevOps, GTM engineering, or sales/marketing ops with a builder profile Deep, hands-on HubSpot experience custom objects, associations, workflows, API —ideally with complex parent-child account structures (multi-location, franchise, healthcare, or roll-up environments) Production experience with Stripe data, including usage-based or non-standard billing models Production experience with Zapier Practical experience building with Claude or comparable LLM APIs, prompting, evaluation, and knowing the failure modes Self-directed; comfortable operating fractionally with async communication and minimal oversight Nice-to-Haves Healthcare or vertical SaaS experience; familiarity with provider data (NPI/NPPES, CMS datasets) Experience supporting multiple concurrent GTM motions (PLG/SMB velocity alongside enterprise sales) dbt and enrichment tooling (Apollo) What You'll Do CRM architecture (HubSpot): The parent-child company model, lifecycle stages, lead routing by segment, workflows, dedup, and data hygiene. You keep the CRM trustworthy so pipeline numbers are real at both the location and parent level. Billing-to-CRM sync (Stripe): Reconcile heterogeneous billing data (subscription, usage, % of collections) with CRM records; surface churn, expansion, and payment signals where the revenue team can act on them. Automation (Zapier + scripting): Build and maintain the integration layer. Know when a Zap is enough and when it's time to write code. Data warehouse (Snowflake): Model GTM and revenue data into clean, queryable tables that handle the hierarchy and mixed pricing models. Strong SQL from scratch. Analytics (Metabase): Dashboards leadership actually uses funnel conversion by motion, pipeline coverage, revenue normalized across pricing models, rollups by parent account. AI workflows (Claude): Lead enrichment and scoring, call summarization, follow-up drafting, and data cleanup at scale, including provider-level enrichment from industry datasets (NPI/NPPES).
